text:
ola: heads-up — seeing a customer repro where cancelling ctx on a streaming request leaves goroutines and connections around. not full hang but connection count slowly creeps up. anyone seen similar with net/http2?
sara: yup. common pattern: req.WithContext(ctx) cancels the stream, we send RST_STREAM, but if resp.Body isn't closed or the server keeps sending, the underlying conn may stay in use. do you have a tiny repro?
ola: gist incoming, but quick summary: Go client (1.20) to our hosted endpoint, streaming response, we cancel after 200ms on slow responses. client does req = req.WithContext(ctx) then go func(){ _, _ = io.Copy(ioutil.Discard, resp.Body); resp.Body.Close() }() in some code paths. still see ~10% leaked sockets after high QPS.
ben: a few pointers: 1) ensure you call resp.Body.Close() on all code paths (even on ctx cancel). 2) set Transport.IdleConnTimeout and call CloseIdleConnections during shutdown. 3) for HTTP/2, ForceAttemptHTTP2=true is default but check you aren't using a custom TLS dialer.
ola: thanks. we already close resp.Body in most places. bumping IdleConnTimeout to 30s didn't change much. curious if http2 stream reset semantics differ — cancel context -> golang sends RST_STREAM, but connection not returned to pool until all streams done?
sara: right — with HTTP/2 a connection is multiplexed so it stays open while other streams are active. RST_STREAM tells server to stop that stream, but if the server doesn't respect it or keeps buffering, you'll still hold resources. also the transport may block reuse if a stream aborted mid-headers.
julia: small checklist I use when debugging: 
- set Transport.TLSHandshakeTimeout, ResponseHeaderTimeout, IdleConnTimeout explicitly
- set MaxIdleConnsPerHost to a reasonable number
- avoid reusing the same Transport across wildly different dialers (custom DialContext vs TLS wrapping)
- instrument with netstat + pprof goroutine dump to see where goroutines are stuck
- try toggling DisableKeepAlives for a quick repro (bad perf but quick test)

ben: another trick — for cancel-heavy short-lived requests you can disable HTTP/2 by setting Transport.TLSNextProto = map[string]func(string, *tls.Conn) http.RoundTripper{} on stdlib transport. then you get per-connection semantics of HTTP/1.1 which sometimes avoids multiplex-related bookkeeping. Not ideal long-term but useful to confirm root cause.
ola: oh interesting. so we can toggle TLSNextProto in staging and see if socket creep stops. will try.
ola: wondering also about the golang.org/x/net/http2 Transport vs stdlib. does anyone prefer one for finer control?
sara: stdlib gained HTTP/2 support and is okay for most. x/net/http2 exposes http2.Transport which gives lower-level hooks (AllowHTTP, DialTLS) that can help if you need to control frames. but it's more manual.
julia: code note: make sure you always set Request = Request.WithContext(ctx) before calling httpClient.Do(req). otherwise cancellation won't wire up. tiny but easy to miss in helper wrappers.
ben: if you have a repro, try this minimal transport tweak when running the load: 
```
tr := &http.Transport{
  TLSHandshakeTimeout: 10 * time.Second,
  IdleConnTimeout: 15 * time.Second,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 250,
  DisableCompression: true,
  // for testing fallback to http1:
  TLSNextProto: map[string]func(string, *tls.Conn) http.RoundTripper{},
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr}
```

then monitor sockets and goroutines.
ola: thanks, will run that. also curious if we should explicitly CloseIdleConnections periodically from our client pool when we detect many cancels. is that sane?
sara: ok for cleanup, yes. it forcibly closes idle connections; won't affect active streams. just be careful about frequent calls (adds churn). best used as emergency mitigation or during shutdown.
ola: quick qol: any flags in our SDK we should expose to customers? IdleConnTimeout & MaxIdleConnsPerHost maybe?
julia: expose timeouts (IdleConnTimeout, ResponseHeaderTimeout) and a 'disable_http2_for_cancel_test' debug flag. plus docs: always use req = req.WithContext(ctx) and read+close resp.Body.
ben: I'll add a tiny checklist to the client README and a sample snippet for streaming cancellation patterns. ola — can you drop the repro gist and results here once you try TLSNextProto toggle?
ola: will do. thanks all. :thumbsup:
infra-bot: Deploy monitor: noticed stage cluster had a 1.3x spike in TCP_CLOSE_WAIT yesterday at 03:14 UTC — correlates with ola's test window. filing infra ticket INF-4321.
ola: filing a bug with repro + heap + goroutine dump and linking INF-4321 shortly. assigning to eng-runtime.
